## Key findings

**The publish shell is genuinely derived, not hand-written.** I re-rendered it from the real stage `cutover.sh` plus the remote-v2 receipt by evaluating the renderer's own f-string AST — byte-identical to the file. So the inherited prefix (project `DEPLOY.lock` via `flock -n 9`, the reviewed preflight) is the one actually proven during preparation. The shell runs three fresh preflights, the third immediately before the single `helm upgrade --atomic --wait`, each asserting Helm 61/deployed, both containers `0f24677…`, one available replica, PVC `7fc2428f`, node Ready/no DiskPressure/no blocking taints, strict `f_bavail*5 > f_blocks`, HTTPS readiness, and 29 feedback rows all `open` with full-row SHA `452929a2…`. No `docker build`/`flutter build`.

**The values/render actually bind the verified image.** My initial concern was that only hashes of server-side files were pinned. `remote-collect-script.sh:52` resolves it: the collector asserted the rendered manifest contains `docker.io/library/quiz-master@sha256:e053b4c4…` exactly twice. Post-upgrade the shell re-checks both containers, one replica, HTTPS, `version.json`, `main.dart.js 9ca6e91b…` and Reader `cfb7188d…`.

**Apparent digest conflict resolved.** The resume guard asserts image id `faef7c1c…` while the packet pins `e053b4c4…`. These are not in conflict: `remote-resume-log.txt:54,74,77` show `e053b4c4…` is the buildx **OCI image-index** digest, which is also the containerd reference and the durable archive content; `faef7c1c…` is failed-v1's local Docker image ID, asserted still present precisely to prove loaded identities were preserved.

**Preparation is real, not a copied marker.** Prepare/guard/collector all exit 0; the `PREPARED` line is printed by the actual script after a real build; the collector independently verified backup 0600 + `integrity_check ok`, rehearsal (`399−263 = 136` new pack rows, originals preserved, rollback and feedback lifecycle ok), copied-DB grading read straight from the rehearsal SQLite (15 finished attempts, 335 score), candidate runtime via `verify_runtime_receipt` at 136/4084/299/180/178, and capacity. failed-v1 is exit 1 and immutable: `20325752832 × 5 < 102417174528` — the guard fired correctly; after cleanup `21124374528 × 5 > total`. No threshold was lowered.

**Executor gates all precede SSH** (`publish_release.py:1–19`): `-O` refusal, refusal to repeat when publish evidence exists, acceptance bound to ACCEPTED/CLI 0/reviewer claude, executor self-hash, packet/shell/package/image equality, callback requiring `accept` + `error_count 0` + the literal packet digest + assignee ≠ reviewer, and an empty diff of `next/quizzes/metadata/study/question_articles` against `9c670e9`. I confirmed that diff is empty against both HEAD `9d0d30bc` and the worktree. The `finally` block preserves partial evidence. The four guard tests pass, exit 0.

**Nothing has been published.** No `execution-acceptance.json`, `publish-log.txt` or `publish-exit.json` exists; baseline remains Helm 61.

## Non-blocking observations (no rework)

1. `publish-preview.sh:67` runs `backup_sqlite.py` but, unlike the prepare path, does not externally re-assert `0600` and `integrity_check` on the new backup. A backup failure still aborts under `set -euo pipefail` before the upgrade, and the verified prepare backup `6794975864…` remains as a restore point.
2. `publish-preview.sh:46–47` checks `nginx.conf` twice — inherited from the stage script, harmless.

I did not execute `publish_release.py` or `publish-preview.sh`, and made no edits, SSH, network, build or Git mutation — only local hash reads, read-only re-rendering, and the four offline guard tests.

I am not claiming deployment occurred or that the 29 open feedback reports are fixed. Published GET/mobile verification, Android, physical screen-reader, a full 20-question run and whole-bank factual certification remain outside this review.
